subject: Geo affinity & streaming requirements — post-demo recap & next actions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Geo affinity & streaming requirements — post-demo recap & next actions

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation, and appreciate the clarity on MedIntel's streaming UX and residency constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same frame for qualification and a pilot timeline.

Recap (high level)
- Primary goal: conversational assistant integrated into clinician workflow with near-real-time streaming (tokenized outputs) and strict PII residency requirements for EU-sourced records.
- Target latency SLOs: p95 token-append latency targets we discussed — US: <= 120ms, EU: <= 160ms, APAC: <= 220ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent streaming sessions during clinic hours, burst to 1,000 concurrent sessions for peak; target sustained aggregate throughput ~1,500 tokens/sec for typical prompt mixes.
- Streaming specifics: client expects sub-100ms visible chunk flush for short-turn responses (first byte within ~200ms for short prompts), and incremental token delivery for long generations.
- Data residency: EU patient-origin data must remain in EU region (processed + logs). APAC data should not be retained in other regions. Audit logs required for SOC2 + upcoming internal audit.

Open/Action items (for Redwood -> MedIntel)
1) SLO matrix: we will produce a one-page SLO matrix mapping p50/p95/p99 for token latency by region + concurrency assumptions (attached: redwood_slo_matrix_v1.xlsx).
2) Tail-latency test plan: proposed load profile + synthetic client for streaming; would you prefer Redwood run tests against your staging endpoint or provide the load generator for your infra team to run?
3) Quantization/model suggestions: initial suggestion is gpt-4o-like open variant (quantized to int8 where acceptable) — need to validate quality vs. cost.
4) Pilot window: MedIntel indicated Jan 2027 is target for a limited pilot. Please confirm a two-week technical validation window in Jan and preferred dates.

Next step: Elliot/Priya — can you share a small representative sample of prompt traces (anonymized) and confirm whether the EU residency means we cannot export any request/response payloads outside the EU (incl. logs)? If you can, please attach a small CSV with typical prompt sizes and expected response lengths.

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik and Grace for capacity and cost estimates.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the EU data residency requirement: any patient-origin data (requests, derived vectors, and full-text logs) must remain within EU-hosted infrastructure; audit logs can be aggregated but cannot include full request payloads outside the EU.

I attached a sample anonymized prompt profile (medintel_sample_profile.csv) — three columns: prompt_token_count, avg_response_token_count, expected_sessions_per_minute. Typical prompts are 30-120 tokens; responses average 60-400 tokens depending on context.

On the test approach: we prefer you provide a Redwood-managed synthetic streaming load generator (docker + simple client) we can run in our staging in the EU so we can validate residency controls and tail latency under realistic network conditions. If you can provide that by Nov 10 we can schedule a staging run the week of Nov 16.

Also — can you confirm whether the proposed quantized variant supports our fine-grained tool-calling flow (we call the tooling on behalf of clinicians and need deterministic tokenization for entity extraction)?

—Elliot

Elliot / Kim — quick technical answers and an action plan below. High level: feasible with the usual tradeoffs; we can meet the targets with a multi-region routing strategy + regional-only processing for EU.

Answers to asks:
- Residency: we can ensure all request/response payloads and request-level logs remain in the EU by deploying a private control plane & regional workers in EU for MedIntel EU traffic. Aggregated, non-identifiable metrics can be exported outside the EU. We will include strict log redaction and retention policy.
- Latency: with a streaming-optimized variant (int8 quantized, kernel-level optimizations) we estimate p95 token-append latency: US ~110–130ms, EU ~140–170ms, APAC ~200–240ms under your sample profile and baseline concurrency. Tail p99 may degrade ~1.5–2x — we’ll include tail mitigation (small dedicated hot shards, prefix caching) in the test plan.
- Concurrency & throughput: for baseline 200 concurrent streaming sessions we recommend a small reserved pool (8x A100-equivalent worker units) with autoscaling headroom for bursts; for the Jan pilot (2-week technical validation) we estimate ~6–8 reserved units for EU and 4 units for US to keep costs reasonable. I’ll convert to a dollar estimate for the proposal.
- Tool-calling / determinism: int8 quantization preserves tokenization determinism; the caveat is model-specific operator reordering — we’ll do a short quality pass on your representative prompts. If any edge cases appear, fallback to a float16 worker for that route is trivial and we can surface a canary route.

Proposed immediate action plan:
1) By Nov 10 — Redwood provides: (a) synthetic streaming load generator (docker + instructions), (b) brief test plan (metrics + thresholds), (c) updated SLO matrix. (drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c_redwood-slo-matrix)
2) Week of Nov 16 — MedIntel runs staging tests in EU (Redwood monitoring & on-call available).
3) Nov 17–21 — Redwood analyzes results and proposes pilot config for Jan (reserved units, model variant, routing policy).
4) Jan 10–24, 2027 — two-week pilot in EU + US with production-like traffic and a rollback plan.

I’ll follow up with a short cost estimate and a draft canary routing policy by EOD Nov 5.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
